text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000002 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity tier, including simple acute visits, but the records came back too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is not confined to sicker patients; it runs at roughly double the all-provider share in every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions. Because risk adjustment already accounts for panel mix, this points more toward a coding habit than a sicker panel, and the low-complexity sample includes 99215s for routine-looking problems such as URI (C0001473, C0002999), UTI (C0000809), back pain (C0000652) and follow-up visits (C0001862). The records review does not confirm this. Only two documented 99215 claims exist, both supported at high MDM, the few lower-level mismatches are too small to weigh, and there is no sign of inflated data-reviewed notes, so the documentation is too thin to judge. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with acute-only diagnoses, and compare C0001661 against C0001959, which the same hypertension patient received as 99215 and 99213 respectively."}
